threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'thank you' to the bus driver. Locals just nod like it’s a secret handshake.
Caught a chat between two blokes on the 196 about their 'successful' late-night kebab hunting. One actually pulled out a laminated map of kebab shops.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a whole street dedicate their front gardens to growing tomatoes – a little patch of Italy in the middle of Neukölln! It felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a döner shop with a resident cat that greets you every time. Makes the late-night snack run feel like home.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Locals know to check the Muni app for delays but just working here still stands at the stop, clueless, as the 14 and 49 toss in a curveball.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo reading Shakespeare on the 31 Union. Only in SF can a late-night bus become a stage.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think we all love the park, but locals know it’s just a good spot to dodge the midday sun and catch a break from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the intricacies of the metro map—still studying it like it's a treasure map.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still flinch when the 38 bus rattles past at 2 AM, while locals are unfazed, chatting away like it's midday.
Last night on the 36, a bloke serenaded the driver with a ukulele. Most of us just stared, but an old lady tapped along with him. Classic Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids transforming a trash bin into a makeshift basketball hoop on the street. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find hidden bars in old public toilets, like 'Klo', where drinks come with a side of nostalgia and curious decor.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're not local if they flinch at the sound of the BART alarms. It's just part of our morning soundtrack.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The Muni bus next to me just broke down mid-street, and a guy in a tuxedo hopped out to direct traffic. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just about Gaudí, missing the small plazas where locals gather for vermut. That’s the real heart of the neighborhood.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they order in cafés, still asking for 'café con leche' instead of just 'café'. It’s the little things.
